residual_disagreements.my_counterclaim: The earlier failure is round-accounting drift plus repair starvation, not ledger growth: the graph spends the round counter before checking convergence and never feeds verifier findings back into the next prompt, so the chassis can terminate early or keep looping blindly before ledger size matters.

Semantic claim-support verification is necessary but not sufficient as the top next move; without injecting verifier findings into the next-round prompt and making agents answer them, a stricter verifier mostly creates more non-converged rounds rather than better repairs.

Peer A1 is correct on the gap (verifier writes ledger entries that never reach next-round prompts, deliberate.py:386-419) but wrong on priority ranking. Piping obligations into prompts BEFORE upgrading what the ledger means produces feedback that says 'address this verified-but-existence-only citation' — agents have nothing actionable to do because the ledger row already says verified=true. Correct order: (1) b8 semantic-support verification so ledger statuses carry signal, (2) A1 obligation loop to route that signal back to agents. Reversing the order ships plumbing without payload.

Partial disagreement: peer A5 is right that budget is not the first failure (max_budget is trace-cumulative, call_contracts.py:136-145) and right that terminal synthesis serializes full position_history (deliberate.py:621-638). But A5 understates per-round ledger growth — verifier_ledger.json appends every citation entry every round and never compacts (verifier.py:559-606), so at max_rounds>5 ledger I/O and resolver hot-path cost grow O(rounds*claims_per_round). First failures, in order: (a) per-round ledger growth, (b) terminal synthesis bloat, (c) drift from agents lacking cumulative verifier state. Drift is third, not first.
